title: Speak, for I hear (1 Samuel 3)
hook: the boy hears his name at night and answers "Speak; for Thy servant heareth"

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hannah's song, the mighty falling and the poor lifted and seated among princes. Your line was raised from the dust. Who did you give a seat to? Today, her son, asleep in the sanctuary. Day seven hundred twenty-nine.

It's night in the sanctuary at Shiloh. The old priest Eli is lying down in his place; his eyes have grown dim. The lamp of God hasn't gone out yet. And the boy Samuel is asleep near the ark. Then a voice says his name. Samuel. He jumps up, runs to Eli: here am I, you called me. Eli says, I didn't call. Lie down again. He lies down. The voice comes again. He runs again. Eli sends him back again. And the text slips in a quiet explanation: Samuel did not yet know the LORD. The word had never been revealed to him. He's hearing a voice he has no way to recognize.
screen: `NIGHT. THE LAMP STILL BURNS.` → `HERE AM I, YOU CALLED ME.` → `HE DIDN'T KNOW THE VOICE YET.`

segments.voice: The chapter opens with a sentence that sets the scene: in those days, the word of the LORD was rare, and visions were not common. So when it finally comes, it comes to a boy who can't tell it from an old man's voice. When the call comes the third time, Eli understands. And here's what the old priest does well. He doesn't take over. He doesn't say, let me handle this. He teaches the boy one sentence and sends him back to bed: if you are called, say, Speak, LORD; for Thy servant heareth. The voice comes, and this time, the text says, the LORD came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. And Samuel answers, "Speak; for Thy servant heareth." Notice that the answer isn't a request. It isn't, give me a sign, or, tell me what I want. It's, I'm here, I'm listening, go ahead. And what he hears is hard. The message is about Eli's own house, judgment on his sons. Samuel lies there until morning, afraid to tell the man who raised him. Eli makes him tell everything, and hide nothing. And Eli answers: it is the LORD; let him do what seems good to him. So the night has two listeners. A boy learning to say speak, and an old man who hears bad news about himself and doesn't look away. The chapter ends with Samuel growing up, and the LORD letting none of his words fall to the ground. The rare word isn't rare anymore. It started with a boy in the dark, saying: speak.
screen: `THE WORD WAS RARE IN THOSE DAYS.` · `ELI TEACHES HIM ONE SENTENCE.` · `A HARD MESSAGE, TOLD WHOLE.` · `NONE OF HIS WORDS FELL TO THE GROUND.` · then, large: `SPEAK; FOR THY SERVANT HEARETH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: listen in the quiet. Tonight, or right now if it's quiet where you are, lie or sit still, and turn the lights down if you can. Don't ask for anything. Just listen. The fridge. A car. Your own breath. Your own thoughts, as they come. If something keeps coming back, a name, a worry, a person you owe a call, let it come. If you pray, you can say Samuel's words, speak, for thy servant heareth, and then stay quiet. If you don't, simply say to yourself: I'm listening. The bell holds the time.
Speak. The word Samuel says in the dark at Shiloh, taught to him by Eli, after he'd heard his name called three times: speak, for your servant is listening. Today's word.
Your line: speak, for I hear. Today, when someone starts to tell you something hard, say some version of it: go ahead, I'm listening. Then actually listen. Day seven hundred twenty-nine.

howItsDone: Jews read Samuel's night call as part of the Former Prophets, and the boy's answer, speak, for thy servant heareth, is read as a picture of what it means to listen for God.

fork.setup: you're Eli. the boy has woken you a third time, sure that you called him. what do you do?
options: tell him firmly to stop dreaming and sleep.
teach him what to answer, and send him back to listen.
go and listen for the voice yourself.
fork.reveal: Eli understands it's God calling, and gives the boy one sentence: speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth. then he lets Samuel hear it himself.

original.note: Hebrew: speak, Samuel's first word back to the voice in the night.

trapdoor: what you thought: a boy hearing voices at night.
what it means: in days when the word was rare, a boy learns to answer, listen, and tell a hard message whole.
what a scholar hears: Eli taught him to say speak, LORD; Samuel answers just speak; for thy servant heareth, without the name.

notes: Audit: howItsDone's unsourced 'is taught to children' generalization softened.
The quotation in 3:10 is given in the index; verify JPS 1917 capitalization ('Thy').
'The third time' is in 3:8; the word segment says he heard his name 'three times' before Eli understood, which follows 3:8. The fourth call is the one he answers (3:10).
'In those days the word of the LORD was rare, and visions were not common' paraphrases 3:1 (JPS 'precious', 'no frequent vision'); not quoted.
No count of words is given for Samuel's answer (an earlier draft miscounted it).
Trapdoor: Samuel's answer omits the divine name Eli told him to use (3:9 vs 3:10). Readers have long noticed this; the trapdoor states only the textual difference.
Original: דַּבֵּר (imperative of the piel dbr), as in 3:9–10. Confirm vocalization and stress.
Editor: 'lies awake' changed to 'lies there' (3:15 says he lay until morning, not that he was awake); 'often' cut from howItsDone under the claims rule.
